text: Leonid Moroz's central chemical evidence for an independent evolutionary origin of the ctenophore nervous system is that ctenophores:
choices: Have no neurons or synapses of any kind
Possess larger, more centralized brains than cnidarians
Use exactly the same neurotransmitters as vertebrates
Lack serotonin, dopamine, and GABA and instead rely on a distinct repertoire including L-glutamate
explanation: Moroz found ctenophores lack serotonin, dopamine, norepinephrine, GABA, and the classical neuropeptides used across cnidarians and bilaterians, relying instead on L-glutamate and a distinct set of peptides, a chemical distinctiveness consistent with independent origin. Ctenophores do have neurons and synapses, do not have larger brains than cnidarians, and their transmitter set differs from that of vertebrates.
